examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 부침개가 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to eat buchimgae on rainy days.
Be careful when you flip a hot buchimgae.
I put plenty of green onions into the buchimgae batter.
This shop's buchimgae is crispy on the outside.
I ate two buchimgae for lunch.

examples.ko: 명절에 온 가족이 모여 부침개도 부쳐요.
examples.en: On holidays the whole family gathers and makes buchimgae too.

explain: 같은 음식을 '전'이라고도 해요. 파전, 김치전처럼 재료 이름 뒤에 '전'을 붙여 말하는 경우가 많고, '부침개'는 일상에서 두루 쓰는 이름이에요. 동사는 '부치다'를 써서 '부침개를 부치다'라고 해요.
explain_en: The same food is also called '전'. People often say '파전' or '김치전' with the ingredient in front, while '부침개' is the general everyday name. The verb is '부치다', so you say '부침개를 부치다' (to pan-fry buchimgae).

examples.en: The dawn sky was tinged with a pale pink.
In spring the cherry blossoms take on a pink tint.

examples.ko: 추운 날 밖에 있었더니 아기 볼이 분홍빛이에요.
examples.en: The baby was outside on a cold day, so its cheeks are pink.
You look bright in that pink dress.

examples.ko: 해 질 무렵 노을이 분홍빛에서 보랏빛으로 변했어요.
examples.en: At sunset the glow changed from pink to purple.
The pink of that flower gets deeper and deeper.

explain: '분홍색'은 색 이름 자체를 말할 때 쓰고, '분홍빛'은 하늘, 볼, 노을처럼 은은하게 번지거나 감도는 색에 잘 어울려요. '붉은빛', '보랏빛'처럼 '-빛'으로 끝나는 짝말이 많아요.
explain_en: '분홍색' simply names the color, while '분홍빛' suits a pink that softly spreads or glows, such as in the sky, cheeks or sunset. There are many matching words ending in '-빛', like '붉은빛' and '보랏빛'.

en: precaution against fire; watching out for fire

examples.en: Being careful with fire is even more important in dry weather.

examples.ko: 겨울이 되면 학교에서 불조심 포스터를 그려요.
examples.en: When winter comes, we draw fire-safety posters at school.

examples.ko: 불조심 기간에 소방서에서 안전 교육을 해요.
examples.en: During fire-safety week the fire station gives safety training.

examples.ko: 집을 비울 때는 불조심을 꼭 하세요.
examples.en: Be sure to be careful with fire when you leave the house.

examples.ko: 산에 갈 때는 불조심에 신경 써야 해요.
examples.en: When you go to the mountains, you have to pay attention to fire safety.
There are signs saying 'Watch out for fire' all over the place.

explain: '불조심하세요'처럼 인사나 주의 말로도 많이 써요. 포스터나 표지판에서는 '꺼진 불도 다시 보자' 같은 표어와 함께 자주 볼 수 있어요. 더 딱딱한 말로는 '화재 예방'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is also used as a warning, as in '불조심하세요'. On posters and signs you often see it with slogans like '꺼진 불도 다시 보자' (check even a put-out fire again). A more formal expression is '화재 예방' (fire prevention).

examples.ko: 불필요한 지출을 줄이려고 구독 서비스를 몇 개 해지했어요.
examples.en: To cut unnecessary spending, I canceled a few subscription services.

examples.ko: 선배가 보고서에서 불필요한 문장을 많이 줄여 줬어요.
examples.en: My senior cut a lot of unnecessary sentences from the report.
That explanation is unnecessary, so you can leave it out.
Leave the unneeded baggage at home.

examples.ko: 이 단계는 불필요하지 않아요. 꼭 해야 해요.
examples.en: This step is not unnecessary. You have to do it.
If you think it's unnecessary, please tell me right away.

explain: 반의어는 '필요하다'예요. 말할 때는 '필요 없다'가 더 자연스럽고, '불필요하다'는 글이나 설명, 회의 같은 자리에서 더 많이 들려요. '쓸데없다'는 더 부정적이고 감정이 들어간 말이에요.
explain_en: The opposite is '필요하다'. In speech '필요 없다' sounds more natural, while '불필요하다' is more common in writing, explanations and meetings. '쓸데없다' is more negative and emotional.

en: being reddish; being tinged with red; red

examples.en: The sunset has a slight reddish tint.
When fall came, the maple leaves turned red.

examples.ko: 해가 질 때 하늘에 붉은빛이 번져요.
examples.en: A red glow spreads across the sky when the sun sets.
The red of this lipstick is too strong.
There are days when the moon looks reddish.
I'm tired, so my eyes look a bit red.

explain: '빨간색'은 분명한 색 이름이고, '붉은빛'은 어떤 것에 붉은 기운이 돌거나 비치는 느낌이에요. '붉은빛을 띠다', '붉은빛이 돌다'처럼 함께 자주 써요.
explain_en: '빨간색' is a clear color name, while '붉은빛' is the feeling of a red tint showing in or on something. It is often used in '붉은빛을 띠다' and '붉은빛이 돌다'.

examples.en: The child played happily, popping soap bubbles.
When the wind blew, the soap bubbles floated up into the sky.
We played with soap bubbles in the park.
Soap bubbles pop right away when you touch them.
A lot of soap bubbles form when I wash the dishes.
I bought my little sibling a bubble toy.

explain: '비눗방울을 불다', '비눗방울을 날리다', '비눗방울이 터지다'처럼 함께 쓰는 동사를 같이 외워 두세요. '거품'은 여러 개가 뭉친 덩어리를 말할 때도 쓰지만, '비눗방울'은 동그랗게 하나씩 뜬 방울이에요.
explain_en: Learn it with its verbs: '비눗방울을 불다' (blow), '날리다' (float up) and '터지다' (pop). '거품' (foam) can be a whole mass of bubbles, while '비눗방울' is a single round bubble floating on its own.

examples.en: When the ambulance came, the cars moved aside.

examples.ko: 좁은 계단에서는 서로 한쪽으로 비켜서면 돼요.
examples.en: On a narrow staircase, you can both step to one side.
I stepped aside for a moment and then walked on.

examples.ko: 문 옆에 비켜서서 사람들이 내리기를 기다렸어요.
examples.en: I stood aside by the door and waited for people to get off.
I stepped to one side, but I still bumped into someone.

examples.ko: 엘리베이터 앞에서 길을 막지 말고 비켜서야 해요.
examples.en: In front of the elevator, don't block the way; you should step aside.

explain: '비키다'는 길에서 몸이나 물건을 옮겨 자리를 내줄 때 쓰고, '비켜서다'는 비켜서 어느 쪽에 서 있는 모습까지 담아요. 부탁할 때는 '좀 비켜 주세요'라고 해요. '비켜!'는 반말이라 무례하게 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: '비키다' means to move out of the way (a body or an object), while '비켜서다' also suggests standing off to one side. When asking, say '좀 비켜 주세요'. '비켜!' is casual speech and can sound rude.

examples.en: When I'm tired, I make sure to take a vitamin supplement.
Swallow this vitamin tablet with water.
I bought a vitamin supplement for my child at the pharmacy.

examples.ko: 비타민제 한 알을 물과 함께 먹어요.
examples.en: I take one vitamin pill with water.

examples.ko: 비타민제도 먹고 있는데 왜 이렇게 피곤할까요?
examples.en: I'm even taking vitamins, so why am I so tired?

examples.ko: 비타민제만 먹지 말고 과일도 많이 드세요.
examples.en: Don't just take vitamins; eat plenty of fruit too.

explain: '비타민'은 영양소 자체를 말하고, '비타민제'는 알약이나 젤리처럼 먹는 제품을 말해요. 일상에서는 '비타민을 챙겨 먹다'라고도 해요. 더 넓게 건강을 위해 먹는 것은 '영양제'라고 해요.
explain_en: '비타민' is the nutrient itself, while '비타민제' is the product you take, such as a pill or jelly. In daily talk people also say '비타민을 챙겨 먹다'. The broader word for health supplements is '영양제'.

examples.ko: 비회원도 이 쿠폰을 쓸 수 있나요?
examples.en: Can nonmembers use this coupon too?

examples.ko: 비회원은 주문 조회 때 전화번호가 필요해요.
examples.en: Nonmembers need a phone number to look up an order.
If you buy as a nonmember, you don't earn points.

examples.ko: 이 도서관은 비회원에게 책을 빌려주지 않아요.
examples.en: This library doesn't lend books to nonmembers.
The nonmember price is higher than the member price.
I'm not a member, so I couldn't get the discount.

explain: 반의어는 '회원'이에요. 쇼핑몰에서 '비회원 구매', '비회원 주문'이라는 말을 자주 봐요. '비-'는 '아닌 사람/것'을 나타내서 '비공개', '비정규직'처럼 많은 말에 붙어요.
explain_en: The opposite is '회원' (member). You often see '비회원 구매' and '비회원 주문' on shopping sites. The prefix '비-' means 'not', and it appears in many words such as '비공개' and '비정규직'.

examples.ko: 두통약은 빈속에 먹지 않는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better not to take headache medicine on an empty stomach.
If I drink coffee on an empty stomach, my stomach burns.
I skipped breakfast, so my empty stomach keeps growling.
If you exercise on an empty stomach, you may feel dizzy.
My stomach is empty, so anything looks tasty.
I ate warm porridge to soothe my empty stomach.

explain: 병원이나 의학 이야기에서는 '공복'이라고 해요. '빈속'은 일상 대화에서 쓰는 말이고, '빈속에'라는 형태로 가장 많이 나와요. 발음은 [빈쏙]이에요.
explain_en: In medical contexts the word is '공복'. '빈속' is the everyday word, and it most often appears as '빈속에'. It is pronounced [빈쏙].

examples.en: On a wet road, a bicycle can slip.
When driving in the rain, you have to slow down.
I was late for the appointment because of the rainy roads.
The car skidded while driving on the wet road.
Please go home carefully on the rainy roads after work.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 오늘 빗길이 많이 미끄러워요.
examples.en: It's raining, so the roads are very slippery today.

explain: '빗길 운전', '빗길 교통사고'처럼 뉴스와 안전 안내에 자주 나와요. 비슷한 짝말로 '눈길', '빙판길'이 있어요. 발음은 [비낄] 또는 [빋낄]이에요.
explain_en: It often appears in news and safety notices, as in '빗길 운전' and '빗길 교통사고'. Similar words are '눈길' (snowy road) and '빙판길' (icy road). It is pronounced [비낄] or [빋낄].

examples.en: Every morning I comb my hair in front of the mirror.
The puppy likes it when I brush its fur.
My hair was tangled, so I combed it for a long time.
A lot of hair came out while I was combing.
Be gentle when you brush a cat.
If you comb your hair before bed, it gets smoother.

explain: 머리를 빗는 일은 '머리를 빗다'가 더 자연스럽고, '빗질하다'는 빗으로 쓸어내리는 동작이나 동물 털을 빗어 줄 때 잘 어울려요. '빗질을 하다'처럼 '을'을 넣어 말할 수도 있어요.
explain_en: For combing hair, '머리를 빗다' sounds more natural, while '빗질하다' fits the motion of running a comb through or brushing an animal's fur. You can also say '빗질을 하다' with '을' in between.

examples.ko: 빨간불에 길을 건너면 안 돼요. 법으로 정해져 있어요.
examples.en: You must not cross the street on a red light. It's the law.
The traffic light turned red, so the car stopped.
When the red light comes on, wait a moment.
The light was red and someone was crossing, so I was startled.
The red light at this crosswalk is too long.
Bicycles also have to stop at a red light.

explain: 반의어는 '파란불'이에요. 신호등의 초록색 불도 한국어에서는 보통 '파란불'이라고 말해요. 정확히 말할 때는 '초록불'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I overworked, and my health started showing warning signs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신호등이 아니라 몸이나 사업, 상황에 '위험하다'는 신호가 나타났다는 뜻이에요. '건강에 빨간불이 켜졌다'가 가장 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is not about a traffic light but means a danger signal has appeared for your body, business or situation. '건강에 빨간불이 켜졌다' is the most common use.
phrases.en_equiv: a red flag; warning signs appear

explain_en: The opposite is '파란불'. Even the green traffic light is usually called '파란불' in Korean, though '초록불' is also used when being precise.

examples.en: The laundry piled up, so I washed it all at once on the weekend.
Please put the dirty laundry in the laundry basket.

examples.ko: 여행에서 돌아와 빨랫감을 한꺼번에 세탁기에 넣었어요.
examples.en: After coming back from the trip, I put all the laundry into the washing machine at once.

examples.ko: 흰색 빨랫감과 색깔 있는 옷을 따로 빨아요.
examples.en: I wash white laundry and colored clothes separately.

examples.ko: 땀에 젖은 운동복을 빨랫감에 넣어 뒀어요.
examples.en: I put the sweaty workout clothes in with the laundry.

examples.ko: 빨랫감 양이 많으면 세제를 더 넣어야 해요.
examples.en: If there is a lot of laundry, you need to add more detergent.

explain: '빨래'는 빠는 일이나 빨아서 널어 둔 옷을 모두 말하고, '빨랫감'은 앞으로 빨아야 할 옷이나 천을 말해요. 그래서 '빨랫감이 쌓이다'라고 하고, '빨래를 널다/개다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '빨래' covers the act of washing and clothes already washed and hung up, while '빨랫감' is the clothes and fabric that still need washing. So you say '빨랫감이 쌓이다' (laundry piles up) but '빨래를 널다/개다' (hang up or fold laundry).

examples.en: I hung the blanket on the clothesline in the yard.
The clothesline is shaking hard in the strong wind.

examples.ko: 빨랫줄 가득 널린 수건이 벌써 말랐어요.
examples.en: The towels hanging all over the clothesline have already dried.

examples.ko: 비가 올 것 같아서 빨랫줄에서 옷을 걷었어요.
examples.en: It looked like rain, so I took the clothes down from the line.
I put up another clothesline on the balcony.
Sparrows are sitting on the clothesline.

explain: '빨래를 빨랫줄에 널다', '빨래를 걷다'처럼 함께 쓰는 동사를 같이 알아 두세요. 요즘 아파트에서는 줄보다 '건조대'에 빨래를 너는 집도 많아요.
explain_en: Learn it with its verbs: '빨래를 빨랫줄에 널다' (hang) and '빨래를 걷다' (take down). In today's apartments, many homes hang laundry on a '건조대' (drying rack) instead of a line.

examples.en: I got a zero on the test and was upset.
If you don't write your name, it's graded as zero.

examples.ko: 빵점 맞은 시험지를 친구가 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend showed me the test paper he got zero on.
I didn't expect to get a zero.
I didn't get a single question right, so it's a zero.

examples.ko: 빵점 받을까 봐 걱정했는데 다행히 아니었어요.
examples.en: I was worried about getting a zero, but luckily I didn't.

explain: '영점'보다 '빵점'이 일상 대화에서 훨씬 편하게 쓰는 말이에요. 반의어는 '만점'이고, '빵점을 받다/맞다'라고 해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 점수와 상관없이 어떤 것이 아주 형편없다고 평가할 때 써요. 주로 '태도가 빵점', '센스가 빵점'처럼 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is used to say something is very poor even when no score is involved, as in '태도가 빵점' or '센스가 빵점'.

explain_en: '빵점' is the casual everyday word, much more relaxed than '영점'. The opposite is '만점' (full marks), and you say '빵점을 받다' or '빵점을 맞다'.

examples.en: My younger sibling is learning addition and subtraction now.
Subtraction is a little harder than addition.
You can solve this problem by subtracting.

examples.ko: 거스름돈을 계산할 때 뺄셈 실력이 필요해요.
examples.en: You need subtraction skills to calculate change.

examples.ko: 아이가 뺄셈 문제를 하나도 안 틀렸어요.
examples.en: The child didn't get a single subtraction problem wrong.
Subtraction was hard, so I used a calculator.

explain: '덧셈', '곱셈', '나눗셈'과 함께 외우면 좋아요. 계산을 읽을 때는 '5 빼기 2는 3'처럼 '빼기'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is good to learn it together with '덧셈', '곱셈' and '나눗셈'. When reading out a calculation, you say '빼기', as in '5 빼기 2는 3'.

examples.en: That person was a fraud who only had smooth words.
I was fooled by a swindler and lost money.
There are many scammers who pretend to be family over the phone.
A swindler is very kind at first.
Don't treat me like a fraud.
Be careful of people who seem like swindlers.

explain: '사기를 치다'는 속이는 쪽, '사기를 당하다'는 속는 쪽이에요. '-꾼'은 어떤 일을 자주 하는 사람을 말해서 '사냥꾼', '일꾼'에도 있어요. 사람에게 쓰면 꽤 심한 말이라서 함부로 말하지 않는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: '사기를 치다' is what the cheater does, and '사기를 당하다' is what the victim goes through. The suffix '-꾼' marks someone who does something often, as in '사냥꾼' and '일꾼'. Calling a person this is quite harsh, so don't say it lightly.

examples.en: When the wind blows, the waves get rougher and rougher.
When a stranger came, the puppy became fierce.

examples.ko: 배가 고프면 고양이가 사나워질 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Cats sometimes get fierce when they are hungry.
The child burst into tears at the angry look on his face.
The weather turned rough, so the plane left late.

examples.ko: 화가 나면 말투가 사나워지는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Some people's way of speaking becomes harsh when they are angry.

explain: '사납다'는 ㅂ 불규칙이라서 '사나워요', '사나운 개'처럼 바뀌어요. 짐승, 날씨, 표정, 말투에 두루 쓰고, 반의어는 '순하다'예요. '거칠어지다'는 피부나 말처럼 부드럽지 않게 된다는 느낌이라 쓰임이 조금 달라요.
explain_en: '사납다' is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it changes to '사나워요' and '사나운 개'. It is used for animals, weather, facial expressions and tone of voice, and its opposite is '순하다' (gentle). '거칠어지다' means becoming rough or not smooth, like skin or speech, so the use is a little different.

examples.en: The hunter chased a deer in the forest.
The hunter climbed the mountain at dawn.
I read a story about a hunter and a tiger.
He is famous as an experienced hunter.
The rabbit chased by the hunter hid in a burrow.
The child who followed the hunter got lost.

explain: 동사는 '사냥하다'이고, 사냥하는 사람을 '사냥꾼'이라고 해요. 옛이야기에서는 '포수'라는 말도 나와요. '-꾼'은 어떤 일을 직업이나 습관처럼 하는 사람에게 붙는 말이에요.
explain_en: The verb is '사냥하다', and the person who hunts is a '사냥꾼'. In old tales you may also see the word '포수'. The suffix '-꾼' is added to a person who does something as a job or habit.

examples.en: I compared the tuition of private and national universities.
My younger sibling got into a private university in Seoul.
I'm looking into scholarships at private universities now.

examples.ko: 이 지역에는 사립대가 세 곳 있어요.
examples.en: There are three private universities in this area.

examples.ko: 사립대 출신이라고 해서 불리한 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Coming from a private university isn't a disadvantage.
My older sister graduated from a private university and joined a company.

explain: '사립대학교'를 줄인 말이고, 짝말은 '국립대'예요. 대학 이야기를 할 때 '사립대'와 '국립대'를 나눠서 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is a short form of '사립대학교', and its counterpart is '국립대' (national university). When people talk about universities, they often divide them into '사립대' and '국립대'.

examples.ko: 목욕탕에 갈 때는 소지품을 사물함에 넣어 두세요.
examples.en: When you go to the bathhouse, put your belongings in a locker.
My gym clothes are in my locker.
I lost my locker key, so I went to the office.
I can't remember my locker number.
This locker opens only when you enter the password.

examples.ko: 헬스장에서 개인 사물함을 한 달 신청했어요.
examples.en: I signed up for a personal locker at the gym for a month.

explain: 학교, 헬스장, 목욕탕처럼 내 물건을 넣어 두는 칸을 말해요. '로커'라고도 하지만 일상에서는 '사물함'이 자주 쓰여요. 지하철역이나 터미널에서 짐을 잠깐 맡기는 곳은 보통 '물품보관함'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the compartment where you keep your own things at school, a gym or a bathhouse. '로커' is also used, but '사물함' is common in daily life. The place in a subway station or terminal where you briefly leave luggage is usually called '물품보관함'.

en: wild greens; mountain greens; mountain herbs

examples.en: In spring people go to the mountains to pick wild greens.
I ordered wild-greens bibimbap for lunch.
These are wild greens that my grandmother picked herself.
We blanch wild greens and season them to eat.
The wild-greens side dishes at this restaurant are tasty.
These wild greens have a slightly bitter taste.

explain: '나물'은 무쳐 먹는 채소 반찬을 두루 말하고, '산나물'은 산에서 자라는 것을 말해요. 고사리, 취나물 같은 것이 대표적이에요. 밭에서 키운 나물과 구분해서 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: '나물' broadly means seasoned vegetable side dishes, and '산나물' are those that grow in the mountains, such as '고사리' (bracken) and '취나물'. It is used to tell them apart from greens grown in fields.

examples.en: Apricots are sweet and sour, so we eat them as jam too.
I bought ripe apricots at the market.
When the apricot blossoms bloom, spring has come.
I drink tea with an apricot scent.
The apricot isn't ripe yet, so it's sour.

examples.ko: 살구 두 개를 깨끗이 씻어서 먹었어요.
examples.en: I washed two apricots well and ate them.

explain: '살구색'은 연한 주황빛 살색을 말해요. 예전에 쓰던 '살색'이라는 말 대신 요즘은 '살구색'을 써요. 비슷하게 생긴 '매실'과는 다른 과일이에요.
explain_en: '살구색' is a light orange, skin-tone color. These days people use '살구색' instead of the older word '살색'. It is a different fruit from the similar-looking '매실' (green plum).

examples.en: Is this problem related to the exam?

examples.ko: 두 사건이 서로 상관있는 것 같아요.
examples.en: The two incidents seem to be related to each other.
They say sleep time and concentration are related.
Age and skill aren't necessarily related.
If it has to do with my work, please let me know.
Are the weather and mood really related?

explain: 보통 '상관이 있다'처럼 '이'를 넣어 말해요. 반의어 '상관없다'는 '괜찮다, 문제없다'라는 뜻으로 '상관없어요'처럼 자주 말해요. '관계있다'와 뜻이 비슷해서 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: People usually say '상관이 있다' with '이' in between. The opposite '상관없다' often means 'it's fine' or 'no problem', as in '상관없어요'. It is close in meaning to '관계있다', and the two can often replace each other.

examples.en: A dove has the symbolic meaning of peace.
This building is a symbolic presence in the city.

examples.ko: 상징적 표현이라서 그대로 이해하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: It's a symbolic expression, so you shouldn't take it literally.
That player's retirement was a symbolic event.
The symbolic meaning of red differs from culture to culture.

examples.ko: 상징적 차원에서 보면 이 행동은 큰 의미가 있어요.
examples.en: Seen on a symbolic level, this action has great meaning.

explain: 뒤에 명사가 와서 '상징적 의미', '상징적 존재'처럼 꾸며요. 서술할 때는 '상징적이에요', 동사를 꾸밀 때는 '상징적으로'라고 해요. '상징', '상징하다'와 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It comes before a noun, as in '상징적 의미' and '상징적 존재'. For a predicate you say '상징적이에요', and to modify a verb, '상징적으로'. It helps to learn it together with '상징' and '상징하다'.

examples.en: I bumped into the door and my little toe hurts.

examples.ko: 새 신발 때문에 새끼발가락에 물집이 생겼어요.
examples.en: The new shoes gave me a blister on my little toe.
I hurt my little toe and went to the hospital.
A hole appeared in the little-toe part of my sock.
The tip of my little toe is red and swollen.

examples.ko: 새끼발가락 쪽이 자꾸 쓸려서 밴드를 붙였어요.
examples.en: The little-toe side keeps rubbing, so I put on a bandage.

explain: 반의어처럼 쓰는 말은 '엄지발가락'이에요. 책상이나 문 모서리에 '새끼발가락을 찧다'라고 많이 말해요. 손에는 짝말인 '새끼손가락'이 있어요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '엄지발가락' (big toe). People often say '새끼발가락을 찧다' (stub your little toe) on a desk or door corner. The matching word for the hand is '새끼손가락'.

examples.en: I made a promise with my friend by hooking little fingers.
I put a bandage on my hurt little finger.
My little finger got caught in the door and swelled up.

examples.ko: 기타를 칠 때는 새끼손가락까지 써야 해요.
examples.en: When playing guitar, you have to use even your little finger.
Only my little finger wouldn't straighten, so I went to the hospital.
Let's hook little fingers and make a firm promise.

explain: '새끼손가락을 걸다'는 약속할 때 하는 행동이라서 한국에서 아이들 사이에서 많이 해요. 다른 손가락은 '엄지', '검지', '중지', '약지'라고 하고, 마지막 손가락만 '새끼손가락'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '새끼손가락을 걸다' (hooking pinkies) is a gesture used when promising, and it is very common among Korean children. The other fingers are '엄지', '검지', '중지' and '약지', and only the last one is '새끼손가락'.

examples.en: I got up at the crack of dawn and went to the airport.
My father goes to work at dawn every day.
I left at dawn, but the roads were still jammed.
It was exam day, so I went to school at dawn.
Today my eyes opened at the crack of dawn.

examples.ko: 새벽같이 시장에 가야 싱싱한 생선을 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to go to the market at dawn to buy fresh fish.

explain: '새벽에'는 시간만 말하지만 '새벽같이'는 아주 일찍 서둘러 움직였다는 느낌이 들어요. '일어나다, 나가다, 오다, 출근하다'처럼 움직임을 나타내는 동사와 자주 써요. 같은 느낌으로 '아침 일찍'이라고도 하지만, '새벽같이'가 더 이르고 부지런한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: '새벽에' only gives the time, while '새벽같이' feels like you moved very early and in a hurry. It is often used with action verbs such as '일어나다', '나가다', '오다' and '출근하다'. '아침 일찍' is a similar expression, but '새벽같이' sounds earlier and more diligent.

examples.en: The baby who woke from dawn sleep started to cry.
I slept badly at dawn, so I'm tired all day.

examples.ko: 옆집 소리 때문에 새벽잠도 제대로 못 잤어요.
examples.en: Because of noise from next door, I couldn't even sleep well at dawn.

examples.ko: 새벽잠 자는 아이를 깨우지 않으려고 살금살금 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked quietly so I wouldn't wake the child sleeping at dawn.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 새벽잠이 없으셔서 늘 일찍 일어나세요.
examples.en: My grandfather doesn't sleep much at dawn, so he always gets up early.
It was so noisy that I couldn't even sleep at dawn.

explain: '아침잠'과 비슷하지만 '새벽잠'은 날이 밝기 전의 이른 시간에 자는 잠을 말해요. '새벽잠이 없다'는 새벽에 일찍 깨서 다시 잘 못 잔다는 뜻으로, 나이가 드신 분들에게 자주 써요. 잠을 잘 못 잘 때는 '잠을 설치다'를 함께 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '아침잠', but '새벽잠' is the sleep in the early hours before daylight. '새벽잠이 없다' means you wake early and can't easily go back to sleep, and it is often said of older people. When you can't sleep well, it goes with '잠을 설치다'.

examples.en: Every morning I hear birdsong outside the window.
Today I woke up to birdsong.
I listened to birdsong while walking along the forest path.
Just listening to birdsong makes my mind feel calm.

examples.ko: 새소리 알람으로 바꿨더니 기분 좋게 일어나요.
examples.en: Since I changed to a birdsong alarm, I wake up in a good mood.

examples.ko: 산에 오르니 새소리 말고는 아무 소리도 안 났어요.
examples.en: When I climbed the mountain, there was no sound except birdsong.

explain: '새소리가 들리다', '새가 지저귀다'처럼 함께 쓰면 자연스러워요. '새 울음소리'라고도 하지만 일상에서는 '새소리'가 더 짧고 흔해요. '새'와 '소리'를 붙여서 한 단어로 써요.
explain_en: It sounds natural in '새소리가 들리다' and '새가 지저귀다' (birds chirp). '새 울음소리' also exists, but '새소리' is shorter and more common in daily life. '새' and '소리' are written together as one word.
